Where it began

Mohammad Abbas was born on 10 March 1990 in Jathekey, a small village near Sambrial, not far from Sialkot. His road into the game was not a quick one. Before he played first-class cricket he worked as a welder in a leather factory, and then as a helper in a Sialkot law firm.

When his chance came, he took it with both hands. He topped the wicket-takers' list in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy of 2015–16 with 61, then did it again the following season with 71.

The player

He first played Test cricket at Sabina Park on 21 April 2017, against the West Indies, and needed only two balls to strike, removing Kraigg Brathwaite. Two Tests later he had his first five-wicket haul. The year 2018 was his: player of the series in England, the PCB's Test Player of the Year and a place in the ICC's Test Team of the Year. Against Australia in the UAE that autumn he reached 50 wickets in his tenth Test, as fast as any Pakistan seamer, and then took five in each innings of the final match.

After three years away from the Test side he returned in South Africa in December 2024, took six wickets in his first game back and bowled Kwena Maphaka for his 100th in the next. In August 2026 he took five for 57 at Lord's. By November 2026 he had played 33 Tests and taken 131 wickets at 22.68, with eight five-wicket innings and one ten-wicket match.

What made him special

Abbas never relied on speed. He ran in at around 75 to 77 miles an hour off an unremarkable run-up that hardly ever varied, delivering from close to the stumps and letting the seam do the talking. His long fingers let him wobble or scramble the seam, so the ball could move either way off the pitch. He gave batters very little to hit, and close to half of his Test victims were bowled or out leg before, which says a great deal about how often he made them play.

With the bat he was a tailender of the honest sort. His 240 Test runs came at 8.57, with a best of 42, and 24 not-outs suggest he was harder to get out than his average lets on.

Away from the middle

English county cricket took to him warmly. He joined Leicestershire in 2018, then moved to Hampshire, where he took a hat-trick against Middlesex in April 2021 and 180 wickets at 19.26 over three seasons. His first game for Nottinghamshire, at Trent Bridge in May 2025, brought five for 31 against Hampshire, and in December 2025 he signed for Derbyshire. At home he played for State Bank of Pakistan from 2023. The ICC named him one of the breakout stars of men's cricket in 2018.

And finally

For a man who took a wicket with his second ball in Test cricket, he never looked in a hurry again. Nothing about his run to the crease looked dramatic. For the batters, that was rather the problem.
